subject: the artifact's mechanically-derived decision field vs the frozen rule

why.frozen_rule: GATE2D_PREREGISTRATION.md section 7 requires, BEFORE entering the precision grid, that the candidate residual be small enough that P2 <= 1e-8 remains theoretically reachable, else FAIL_REPRESENTATION; section 22 adds FAIL_REPRESENTATION if degree 16 is insufficient and a higher degree would be needed.
why.degree_needed_for_relative_target: eps_cand would have to fall from 1.93e-07 to ~2.4e-16 for the RELATIVE target to be reachable; the degree-20 tail is ~8e-10, so roughly degree 35-40 would be required. Degree 16 is insufficient for a relative criterion on this function.
why.conclusion: the representation, not the precision grid, is what fails; FAIL_WITHIN_GRID would mis-name the cause

implementation_defect_recorded_not_patch.defect: sr_realcandidate.py computes acceptance_precondition AFTER the precision cells and never branches on it, so the frozen section-7 gate was not enforced in code. The decision field therefore fell through to the selection rule.
implementation_defect_recorded_not_patch.blast_radius: naming only. Both outcomes are failures; the artifact records the measured precondition value, so the frozen rule is applied on top of the artifact rather than against it.
implementation_defect_recorded_not_patch.not_patched_because: no post-T2 mutation is permitted. A test asserts the module is byte-identical to its T1 hash.
implementation_defect_recorded_not_patch.fix_for_the_successor: evaluate and branch on the acceptance precondition BEFORE the grid, as section 7 specifies, and assert that ordering in a pre-T2 test.

what_did_NOT_fail.precision: P2 equals P2_floor at 256, 384 and 512 bits; the interval radius runs 1.11e-55 -> 2.81e-94 -> 6.09e-132 and is irrelevant to the outcome
what_did_NOT_fail.conditioning: the genuine candidate loses 30.54 digits against unit_candidate's 50.96 measured in the SAME run -- 20.4 digits BETTER

root_cause.statement: P2 is a RELATIVE half-width, and Gate-2A calibrated it on unit_candidate whose panel integral is |acc| = 75.94. A genuine backward function has a huge dynamic range across the SR square: h_1 runs from ~1e-9 near a = 0 to 0.63 at a = b_SR, and its panel integral at patch (17,11) is |acc| = 3.75e-9. The same ABSOLUTE enclosure error (~1.3e-10) therefore reads as a relative 3.54e-02.
root_cause.not_separability: the NON-separable h_2 probe fails by the same mechanism (|acc| = 9.04e-06, P2 = 6.96e-06 = its floor), so the cause is function SCALE, not separability

probe_caveat: the non-separable probe's node values were enclosed by acb.integral at 256 bits, so its coefficient radii do not shrink with evaluation precision; its 512-bit digit-loss figure (86.55) is a construction artifact and only its 256-bit figure is meaningful. It is non-decisive in any case.
consequence: Gate-2A's SR precision conclusion is NOT invalidated -- with a real candidate the conditioning is better, so 256 bits remains supported on that axis. What is invalidated is the P2 acceptance INSTRUMENT: a relative criterion cannot be applied to real backward functions spanning nine orders of magnitude. That is a new named gap, and it must be re-specified BEFORE a successor gate runs, with a justification independent of any result.
